S0.title: Original Slay the Spire knowledge (research lead only, never STS2 evidence)

mechanics.name: Energy
mechanics.description: Per-turn resource spent to play cards; cards declare an energy cost. Exact starting amount and per-turn refill rule for STS2 not confirmed in gathered sources.
mechanics.timing: on card play; refill at start of player turn (assumed)
interactions: M.stars competes with energy for card affordability on Regent cards
counterexamples: Regent cards may need both Energy and Stars
X-cost cards consume all remaining energy (STS1 behavior; STS2 not confirmed)
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Turn structure
mechanics.description: Player turn then enemy turn alternate; draw, play, discard-end-of-turn loop. Specific hand size, draw count and starting energy for STS2 are unverified.
effects: non-Retain cards discarded at end of turn
mechanics.timing: start of player turn / end of player turn / enemy turn
interactions: M.poison ticks at start of the poisoned creature's turn per S6
M.doom checks at end of enemy turn per S1/S7
counterexamples: Do not hardcode 5 cards / 3 energy as STS2 facts
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)
mechanics.gap: initial draw count, hand limit, base energy not source-confirmed

mechanics.name: Combat end conditions
mechanics.description: Combat ends when all enemies are dead (player wins) or player HP reaches 0. Doom kills count as deaths at end of enemy turn.
counterexamples: Doom and Poison deaths occur at their own timings, not immediately on play
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Hand size limit
mechanics.description: Whether STS2 caps hand size and what happens to overflow draws is not confirmed.
counterexamples: Do not assume a 10-card cap
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Exhaust
mechanics.description: An Exhausted card moves to the Exhaust pile until end of combat. Cards usually exhaust themselves when played; some effects exhaust other cards. Return from the Exhaust pile is limited, typically by playing directly from it.
preconditions: card has Exhaust or effect exhausts it
mechanics.timing: on play (self) or on triggering effect
interactions: M.sly and discard loops do not recycle exhausted cards
synergy with exhaust-payoff cards (unspecified)
counterexamples: Exhausted cards return to deck next combat (deck is reset each combat)
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Retain
mechanics.description: Retained cards are not discarded at end of the player's turn and stay in hand until played, discarded or exhausted.
effects: card stays in hand at end of turn
interactions: Sovereign Blade is a Retain colorless attack
counterexamples: Hand-limit behavior with many retained cards unverified
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Innate
mechanics.description: Keyword listed in STS2 keyword glossaries; semantics presumed to be 'starts in opening hand'.
counterexamples: Do not rely on exact multi-Innate overflow behavior
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Sly
mechanics.description: If a Sly card is discarded from hand during the player's turn, it plays for free. Silent's signature keyword.
effects: card is played for free (no energy)
mechanics.timing: on discard event during player's turn
interactions: triggers on any discard source (card effects)
not triggered by end-of-turn discard (wording: 'before the end of your turn')
counterexamples: End-of-turn hand discard does not trigger Sly per wording (inferred)
Targeting of auto-played Sly attacks unverified
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Discard (effect)
mechanics.description: Moving a card from hand to discard pile by effect. Triggers Sly. Pile mechanics otherwise as per turn cycle.
interactions: M.sly triggers on it
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Card upgrade
mechanics.description: Upgrading permanently improves a card for the run. Rest Site option is named Smith (wiki.gg) or Forge (a routing guide); Smith is likelier official naming. Forge is a separate Regent keyword.
interactions: M.rest_site competes_for the same node with healing
counterexamples: Do not confuse Smith with the Regent Forge keyword
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Attack damage resolution
mechanics.description: Attack deals damage to Block first, remainder to HP. Modifiers: Vulnerable (+50% taken), Weak (-25% dealt). Order of Strength, Weak, Vulnerable and rounding in STS2 is unverified; STS1 order was (base+Strength) then Weak then Vulnerable, rounded down.
interactions: each hit of a multi-hit attack resolves separately against block
Doom and Poison are not attacks and bypass block
counterexamples: Poison/Doom do not go through this pipeline
Unblockable or armor-like mechanics unverified
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Block
mechanics.description: Block absorbs incoming attack damage 1:1 and expires at the start of the owner's next turn unless a relic or power says otherwise. Does not stop Poison, Doom or other non-attack loss.
effects: reduces incoming attack damage by amount
expires at owner's next turn start
mechanics.timing: applies at damage resolution; expiry at start of owner's turn
interactions: counters attacks, not Poison/Doom
Frail/Dexterity change gained amount
counterexamples: Osty HP is not Block and does not reset (S11)
Retention relics/powers exist (specific ones unverified)
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Vulnerable
mechanics.description: Target takes 50% more damage from attacks for X turns.
mechanics.duration: X turns, duration decays per turn (decay timing unverified)
mechanics.stacking: stacks add duration (inferred); strength fixed at +50%
interactions: boosted by cards that make Vulnerable/Weak 'twice as effective' (S5 card list)
Vicious: draw on applying Vulnerable (S7)
counterexamples: Does not affect Poison or Doom
Magnitude can be altered by specific cards/relics
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Weak
mechanics.description: Affected creature's attacks deal 25% less damage for X turns.
interactions: boostable like Vulnerable (S5)
counterexamples: Does not reduce non-attack damage
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Frail
mechanics.description: Glossary claims Frail reduces Block gained by ~25%. Single low-quality source.
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Strength
mechanics.description: Adds damage to attacks; lasts the combat per glossaries. Exact numeric rule not sourced from STS2 wiki here.
interactions: scales multi-hit attacks per hit
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Dexterity
mechanics.description: Adds Block to Block-granting cards; lasts the fight per glossary.
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Focus (Defect)
mechanics.description: One source says Focus is now mostly temporary and per-turn rather than permanent. Treat as version_dependent.
counterexamples: Do not assume STS1 permanent Focus
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Poison
mechanics.description: Poisoned creature loses HP each turn and Poison decreases by 1 per tick. Ignores Block. Timing: one fan site says start of the poisoned creature's turn. Accelerant buff triggers Poison X additional times.
mechanics.timing: start of poisoned creature's turn (S6; unconfirmed on wiki.gg)
interactions: ignores Block
Accelerant adds extra triggers
Potion applies Poison (6 in S5)
some cards conditionally apply more if target already poisoned
counterexamples: Not an attack: Vulnerable/Strength do not apply
Total damage from N stacks = N(N+1)/2 if it ticks to 0 with no extra triggers (inferred)
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)
mechanics.gap: exact timing vs STS1; behavior on enemy death/fight end

mechanics.name: Doom
mechanics.description: At end of the afflicted creature's turn (wiki.gg) / end of all enemies' turns (sts2wiki.org), if Doom >= current HP, it dies. Kills without modifying HP, so it ignores Block, Slippery and Intangible. Necrobinder signature.
mechanics.timing: end of enemy turn (exact phrasing varies by source)
interactions: bypasses Block/Slippery/Intangible
Potion of Doom applies 33 (S5)
can pair with HP-reduction to bring HP under Doom
counterexamples: Boss low-HP triggers may be bypassed (one fan site claims); unverified
Enemy that heals after applying Doom raises threshold
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)
mechanics.conflict: S1 says end of their turn; S7 says end of all enemies' turns

mechanics.name: Slippery and Intangible
mechanics.description: Named on wiki.gg as defensive effects that Doom ignores. Their own rules are not gathered.
counterexamples: Do not assume STS1 Intangible (damage capped to 1) for STS2 values
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Osty (Necrobinder companion) and Summon
mechanics.description: Necrobinder gets companion Osty at combat start (1 HP initially). Osty takes damage before the Necrobinder, gains HP via Summon effects, only one Osty can exist, and if destroyed returns next turn. Osty's HP is not Block and does not reset at end of turn.
mechanics.timing: summoned at combat start; revive start of next turn
interactions: competes with Block as damage absorption
Osty attack cards deal damage via Osty (details unverified)
counterexamples: Overflow damage beyond Osty HP to player: unverified
Osty HP at combat start differs across sources (1 HP vs fixed)
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)
mechanics.gap: overflow behavior, Osty max HP, Osty damage scaling

mechanics.name: Souls and Graveyard
mechanics.description: Necrobinder cards generate Souls and depend on Souls for damage/Block/Summon. One article calls it the most risk-reward mechanic. Rules unverified.
counterexamples: No rule-level evidence
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Stars (Regent)
mechanics.description: Regent's persistent secondary resource: does not reset at turn end, reportedly uncapped, spent by cards, many Regent cards cost both Energy and Stars.
mechanics.timing: gained by cards/relics; no end-of-turn reset
interactions: Star Potion exists
competes_for card affordability with energy
counterexamples: Cross-combat persistence not stated
Cap claim from single fan site
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Forge and Sovereign Blade

interactions: Retain lets the blade accumulate in hand
Sovereign Blade scales with upgrades/synergy per one guide
counterexamples: Distinct from Rest Site 'Smith/Forge' naming

mechanics.name: Map and room types
mechanics.description: Each act is a branching map with room types: Monster, Elite (extra relic), Rest, Merchant, Unknown (?: events, sometimes shops/fights), Treasure, Boss; each act opens with an Ancient (Neow in Act 1). Last room before each boss is a Rest Site. Act 3 can end with double boss at Ascension 10.
interactions: path choice competes_for HP/gold/upgrades
counterexamples: Winged Boots/Golden Compass change path rules
Alternate acts exist (Overgrowth/Hive named)
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Rest Site
mechanics.description: Choose Rest (heal 30% of max HP rounded down per wiki.gg; some guides say 30% of missing HP — conflict) or Smith (upgrade a card). Rest available at full HP. Relics add options or effects (Regal Pillow +15 HP, Stone Humidifier +5 max HP when resting, Tiny Mailbox potion, Dream Catcher card reward). Unaffected by Ascension since v0.103.2.
interactions: competes_for node choice: heal vs upgrade
counterexamples: Relics can unlock multiple options
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)
mechanics.conflict: heal basis: max HP (S2) vs missing HP (S12)

mechanics.name: Merchant (shop)
mechanics.description: Buy cards, relics, potions and one card removal with Gold. Reported potion prices: Common 48-53, Uncommon 71-79, Rare 95-105. Card removal 75 gold in one guide (base price unverified; Ascension 6 'Inflation' makes removal costlier). Foul Potion thrown at Merchant gives 100 gold.
interactions: Maw Bank gives 12 gold per floor until gold is spent at shop
Lord's Parasol takes everything free
counterexamples: Purchases fail without potion slots
Removal price may rise over run (unverified)
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Unknown-room events
mechanics.description: Events offer trade-offs (HP, gold, cards, relics, potions, curses). Examples with explicit effects: Sunken Treasury (small chest gold / large chest more gold plus permanent curse). Event pools vary by act/region.
counterexamples: Event content varies by act; parse option text at runtime
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Ancients and boons
mechanics.description: Each act begins with an Ancient. After Act 1/2 bosses Ancient heals 100% of missing HP (80% on Ascension 2+) and offers three Ancient relics. Boss rewards: 100 gold (75 at A3+), choice of three rare cards, sometimes a potion.
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Gold economy
mechanics.description: Gold from combat victories, events, relics; spent at shops. Ectoplasm blocks gold gain; Seal of Gold converts 3 gold to energy per turn.
interactions: competes_for removal vs relic vs potion
counterexamples: Some relics make gold unspendable or unobtainable
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Potions and slots
mechanics.description: Potions are single-use consumables held in limited slots; Potion Belt adds 2 slots. Examples: Block Potion 12, Vulnerable Potion 3, Weak Potion 3, Poison Potion 6, Potion of Doom 33. Base slot count not gathered.
interactions: competes_for slot space with newly found potions
counterexamples: Base slot count unverified
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Ascension
mechanics.description: Difficulty modifiers that change numbers (e.g., boss gold, Ancient heal, shop removal cost). Changes between patches.
mechanics.game_version: STS2 Early Access (exact build unknown; sources cite patches v0.100.0-v0.103.2)

mechanics.name: Deck building economy
mechanics.description: Add cards from rewards, remove at shop/events, upgrade at rest. Strategic content is guide-derived, not rules. Rules: boss reward offers rare choices; shop offers removal.
counterexamples: Guide strategy claims are heuristics, not mechanics
